name: shellbags
description: Walk BagMRU in UsrClass.dat or NTUSER.DAT and return the folders a shell opened on this account: the reconstructed path, the key's last-write time (raw FILETIME and ISO), the shell item's own DOS timestamps (local time, to two seconds) and the MRU order. It reaches folders on devices and shares that are long gone; it does not say who opened them. Every BagMRU root the hive has is walked and named (the Shell and ShellNoRoam trees can both be populated) and each entry says which; a numbered value with no key under it is decoded and listed under values_without_subkey, not dropped; values are read whole (regipy's default cut to 128 bytes is not taken). A shell item's long name is read from its layout only for the file entry extension (0xbeef0004) versions 3, 7, 8 and 9, at the offset the libfwsi notes give for the version (0x14, 0x26, 0x2A, 0x2E), bounded by the block's declared size, and only when the block's own name offset (the 2-byte field at 0x10) agrees and what is there is a printable string that ends inside the block (long_name_from: layout, extension_layout: decoded; a localised name after it, where there is one, is localized_name); in any other case the long name is the longest string found in the block, labelled long_name_from: strings with extension_layout saying why the layout was not applied, a candidate and not a decode. Every list of subkeys and values is read through the size of the hive: a hive of N bytes holds at most N/76 keys and N/20 values, so an index that repeats one list (an ri element named again and again) is read to that bound, listed once per key, and said under problems; it is not followed. A key whose subkey list was already walked (a cycle) is a problem, not walked again; a shell item that cannot be decoded is listed as undecodable. Other shell item classes are string candidates (decoded: strings). max_depth is 1 to 128; keys below it are listed under not_walked_below_max_depth, and problems are a page. The tool stops at its own time limit (115 seconds) and names the keys it did not walk (status partial); SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON and no temporary file. Result files are named from the hive, the roots and whether contains was given, never from the needle, and are never replaced (another needle takes the next free -n name). The library's own messages, which can hold bytes of a name, are counted and never printed. Every answer carries status and status_basis. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (shell item names, paths and registry keys): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a piece of 12 characters of a secret that two cuts left behind is caught) (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at, by the keys on the way as they are shown or by positions, never by a withheld key). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text, by both layers and by the backstop on its own; hexadecimal with no secret-shaped text in it is shown as it is, random bytes included (a binary key is printed). A filter on content (contains) is applied to the text that is shown, never to what is withheld: what it did not match and has text withheld in it is counted (contains_blind_entries) and makes the answer partial, because the needle may be in what is withheld; the count is the same whatever the needle is. write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on random plants of every shape in 13 slots (988 per shape; the tests plant them again): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys (one line and several), connection strings, user-info (an @, a / or a + inside the password, a random user of any length, a GitLab token glued to hexadecimal digits), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, upper-case and glued prefixes, AWS-shaped secret keys of 40 characters: none printed whole and no piece of 12 characters of one printed; 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys: at most 0.1% overall (worst slot 1.3%); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters: at most 0.4% overall (worst slot 2.6%); random lower-case letters of 24: 8.5% overall, 16% in the worst slot; a 16-character base32 seed: 11% overall, 18% in the worst slot. In a binary slot (a hexadecimal REG_BINARY value or table cell) the backstop decodes the hexadecimal and replaces every hex-encoded shape it claims (480 of 480 plants), but random bytes that hold no text are printed (200 of 200), and so is a hexadecimal secret written as text there (a 32-digit one in a table cell: 97%). Real Windows strings changed (any part withheld) in 9,950 generated registry, file, service, package and host names, SIDs, GUIDs and typed digests (2 changed: the 32-digit hash in a Chrome and an Edge autolaunch value name) and 3,431 strings of real event logs (25 changed: 17 of 1,040 whole event records, 7 of 313 command lines and messages, 1 of 322 path fields; they hold encoded PowerShell payloads and the 32-digit hash directories of the .NET native-image cache). Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more (handles, a Chrome field-trial handle, a mojo pipe name), unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more (the native-image directories), and the query values of a URL in a URL slot. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name or of any length in a binary slot, anything under 16 characters in a name; 75% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true.

hive.description: An extracted UsrClass.dat (or NTUSER.DAT for the older location)

key.description: Override the BagMRU root when the hive puts it somewhere unusual (then only that root is walked)

contains.description: Keep only paths containing this string, case-insensitive; the text is looked at as shown, so a needle inside withheld text matches nothing and what it did not match but has text withheld is counted and makes the answer partial

max_depth.description: How deep to walk (default 24, at most 128); a key below it that has subkeys is named in not_walked_below_max_depth

limit.description: Entries shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); the whole tree is walked, and when more entries match the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
